hypothesis: The security bottleneck in NL->on-chain-invariant translation is not generation but FAITHFULNESS VERIFICATION, and the autoformalization-of-mathematics evidence implies that a deterministic round-trip / equivalence-selection gate (back-translate the candidate predicate to NL and/or accept only when k independent candidates are provably equivalent) will catch a large fraction of unfaithful predicates that humans and single-shot LLM review miss. Concretely: requiring symbolic-equivalence agreement among k>=3 independently sampled candidate predicates before a predicate may be deployed will reduce the rate of semantically-wrong-but-compilable invariants by a large margin versus accepting the top-1 generation.
rationale: Adjacent-field (mathematics autoformalization) evidence repeatedly locates the trust problem in the NL->formal step, not the prover/checker. 'Autoformalization with Large Language Models' reports that even strong LLMs perfectly formalize only ~25% of competition statements, so most single-shot outputs are wrong despite being syntactically valid Isabelle/HOL - the on-chain analogue is a compilable-but-unfaithful invariant. 'Autoformalize Mathematical Statements by Symbolic Equivalence and Semantic Consistency' documents a large pass@1-vs-pass@k gap and recovers faithful formalizations by scoring candidates with (a) symbolic equivalence checked by an automated theorem prover and (b) semantic consistency via back-translation - both of which are DETERMINISTIC checks suitable for an on-chain or replayable gate. 'nl2spec' independently shows that mapping subformulas back to NL fragments exposes and lets users repair the inherent ambiguity of requirements. 'Consistent Autoformalization for Constructing Mathematical Libraries' shows reliability degrades as domain specialization grows (DeFi invariants are highly specialized) and is recovered by retrieval + syntax-error auto-correction feedback loops. Together these imply that the division of labor in Q2 (off-chain LLM generation, deterministic gate) should place an EQUIVALENCE/ROUND-TRIP CHECK at the gate, not merely a type/compile check.
supports_if: An ablation on a benchmark of NL DeFi-intent -> invariant predicate shows that a k-candidate symbolic-equivalence + back-translation selection gate reduces semantically-wrong-but-compilable predicates substantially (e.g. >2x) relative to top-1 selection, with the residual errors dominated by cases the equivalence check cannot decide (timeouts / undecidable fragments) rather than by faithfulness slips.
refutes_if: k-candidate equivalence selection and back-translation provide little or no improvement over top-1 plus compile/type checking (LLM errors are correlated across samples so candidates agree on the SAME wrong predicate), OR the deciding equivalence check is so often intractable/undecidable for the invariant representation that the gate degenerates to compile-checking, leaving faithfulness unguarded.
motivating_papers: Autoformalize Mathematical Statements by Symbolic Equivalence and Semantic Consistency
nl2spec: Interactively Translating Unstructured Natural Language to Temporal Logics with Large Language Models
Consistent Autoformalization for Constructing Mathematical Libraries

hypothesis: The neurosymbolic-reasoning and program-synthesis-with-feedback literatures imply that the secure architecture is a strict LLM-as-semantic-parser / deterministic-engine-as-arbiter split, and crucially that the SOLVER'S ERROR MESSAGES (not human review) are the highest-leverage faithfulness and robustness signal. Therefore an on-chain (or deterministic, replayable) checker that returns structured, machine-readable rejection reasons into an off-chain self-refinement loop will outperform both pure-LLM generation and human-in-the-loop review on adversarial robustness of the deployed invariant - because the deterministic gate is the only component an adversary cannot prompt-inject.
rationale: In Logic-LM the LLM only translates NL into a symbolic formulation while a DETERMINISTIC symbolic solver performs the inference, yielding +39.2% over plain LLM and +18.4% over chain-of-thought; the paper's self-refinement module feeds the solver's error messages back to revise the formalization. LINC makes the same claim sharper: the LLM acts purely as a semantic parser and an external first-order theorem prover does the sound deductive step, fixing the 'subtle and unpredictable' failures of LLM-internal reasoning. This is structurally identical to bloom's Q2 division of labor (off-chain LLM generation + deterministic on-chain gate): the trustworthy, attacker-resistant component is the deterministic engine, and the LLM is a hint generator whose output is never trusted directly. 'Towards AI-Assisted Synthesis of Verified Dafny Methods' and 'PropertyGPT' extend this to verification artifacts specifically: PropertyGPT uses compilation/static-analysis feedback as an external oracle to iteratively repair generated properties (compilable / appropriate / verifiable), and Dafny synthesis improves sharply when the verifier's signal is in the loop. The cross-disciplinary inference is that faithfulness AND adversarial robustness both reduce to making the deterministic checker's verdict the only thing that gates deployment, and exposing its diagnostics as the refinement signal.
supports_if: A pipeline where a deterministic checker emits structured rejection reasons consumed by an off-chain refinement loop produces deployed invariants with both higher faithfulness and higher resistance to adversarial NL intents (intents crafted to smuggle a vacuous/always-true predicate past review) than (a) one-shot LLM generation and (b) LLM generation with human review but no machine diagnostic loop; and prompt-injection attempts in the NL intent fail to alter the gate's verdict because the gate never reads NL.
refutes_if: Closing the deterministic-checker feedback loop yields no robustness gain over human review, OR adversarial intents succeed by producing predicates that PASS the deterministic gate yet violate human intent (e.g. trivially-satisfiable or scope-mismatched invariants the gate cannot distinguish), showing the deterministic engine cannot by itself separate faithful from adversarially-vacuous predicates and that social/economic arbitration is unavoidable for the residual.
motivating_papers: Logic-LM: Empowering Large Language Models with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning

Towards AI-Assisted Synthesis of Verified Dafny Methods

hypothesis: The model-checking / temporal-logic-synthesis and requirements-engineering evidence implies that the best shared referent between human, LLM, and on-chain checker is NOT free-form first-order/temporal logic but a CONSTRAINED, PATTERN-TEMPLATED predicate representation over a DECIDABLE, FINITE-TRACE fragment - because that simultaneously delivers Q3's required properties (totality, determinism, bounded resources via guaranteed-terminating evaluation, and decidable equivalence for canonical identity) AND maximizes human comprehension, which the same literature shows is otherwise alarmingly poor. Free-form logical representations will exhibit a measurable human-misreading rate high enough to make them unsafe as the human-facing referent even when machine-faithful.
rationale: From the model-checking side, 'First-Order Temporal Logic on Finite Traces: Semantic Properties, Decidable Fragments, and Applications' establishes that restricting to finite traces and identified decidable fragments yields ExpSpace-complete (i.e. DECIDABLE) satisfiability - the property needed for canonical identity and decidable equivalence of on-chain predicates, and finite-trace semantics matches a blockchain's finite, deterministic execution history (bounded resources / totality). But decidability is necessary, not sufficient, for a SHARED referent: 'On the Understandability of Temporal Properties Formalized in Linear Temporal Logic, Property Specification Patterns and Event Processing Language' provides direct adjacent-field evidence that humans systematically misread formalized temporal properties and that representation choice (raw LTL vs. specification patterns) significantly changes comprehension accuracy. The requirements-engineering thread ('nl2spec') reinforces that ambiguity is inherent in NL and must be surfaced at the level of small, named sub-formulas humans can validate. The cross-disciplinary synthesis: pick the representation at the intersection of a decidable finite-trace fragment (machine side) and a bounded library of named, audited patterns/templates (human side); a referent that is decidable but free-form will fail on the human axis, and one that is human-friendly prose will fail on the machine axis.
supports_if: In a head-to-head study, expressing the same invariants as named patterns over a decidable finite-trace fragment yields (a) higher human accuracy at judging whether a predicate matches a stated intent than free-form logic, and (b) tractable, total, deterministic on-chain evaluation with computable canonical forms / decidable equivalence within resource bounds - whereas a more expressive free-form representation either becomes undecidable for equivalence or shows a high human misread rate.
refutes_if: The pattern/decidable-fragment restriction is too weak to express common DeFi invariants (forcing escape into an undecidable or non-total full logic to remain faithful), OR human comprehension does not differ between templated and free-form representations (so constraining the representation buys machine properties at no human-side benefit and the 'shared referent' framing collapses to a purely machine-side decidability question).
